review_notes:
I read the whole file. I checked these declarations against Mathlib: PowerSeries.liftOfIsAdicComplete (plus Aux and helper lemmas), coeffwiseIdeal, isPrecomplete_map_mk, Submodule.eq_top_of_isAdicComplete_of_fg_of_sup_smul_eq_top, IsIntegrallyClosed.of_faithfullyFlat, smul_injective_of_flat, and the abbrevs Rh, mh and W.

The closest competitor is Mathlib's PowerSeries.eval₂Hom / PowerSeries.aeval in Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Evaluation.lean. It needs uniform and topological structure, HasEval, and a continuous coefficient map, and Mathlib's AdicCompletion files have no HasEval bridge. The file's lift is ideal-based and is built on Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom, so replacing it would add conversions rather than remove duplication. I abstained on that one.

I found no Mathlib definition matching coeffwiseIdeal or the quotient-precompleteness lemma. The faithfully-flat descent of integral closure and the Nakayama-style statement are standalone theorems, which the rubric excludes, and I found no Mathlib counterpart for them anyway. The same lift lemmas also appear in another solution file (S_PowerSeries_existsUnique_ringHom_of_isAdicComplete.lean). That looks like a per-problem packaging artifact, so I did not treat it as a Mathlib-concept duplication. I did not read the imported project files.
